# load libraris

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
```

# import data

```{r}
gss<- read.csv("gsssubset.csv")
head(gss)
```


# double filter filtering
# single filter

```{r}
single_filtered<-gss %>% 
  filter(marital=="MARRIED")
head(single_filtered)
```


# double filter

```{r}
double_filtered<-gss %>% 
  filter(marital=="MARRIED"|
           marital=="DIVORCED")
head(double_filtered)
```




# multiple filtering
```{r}
gss_degree <- gss %>%
  filter(
    degree %in% c("BACHELOR", "GRADUATE", "JUNIOR COLLEGE"),
    marital %in% c("MARRIED", "DIVORCED"),
    sex %in% c("MALE"),
  
    )
  

head(gss_degree)
```



# data format
# long/wide format

# sample data set
```{r}
grades_wide<- tibble(
  student=c("alice", "Bob", "charlie"),
  math_2023=c(85, 92, NA),
  math_2024=c(88, 90, 85),
  science_2023=c(78, NA, 80),
  science_2024=c(82, 85, 88)
  
)
head(grades_wide)
```

# pivot_longer
- its purpose is to reduce the number of columns while keeping original info
```{r}
grades_long<-grades_wide |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols=-student,
    names_to=c("subject", "year"),
    names_sep="_",
    values_to="score",
   
  )
head(grades_long)
```




# pivot wider> long to wide format
```{r}
grades_wide_back<- grades_long %>% 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from=c("subject", "year"),
    names_sep="_",
    values_from=score
  )
head(grades_wide_back)
```



# advanced joints
```{r}
df1<-tibble(
  id=c(1, 2, 3, 4),
  name=c("alice", "Bob", "charlie","David"))

df2<-tibble(
  id=c(2, 3, 5),
  score=c(85,90, 78)
)
```


# join types
# inner_join(): common matching keys, unique

```{r}
inner_join(df1, df2, by="id")
```



# full_join()
```{r}
full_join(df1, df2, by="id")
```



# semi-join
```{r}
semi_join(df1, df2, by="id")
semi_join(df2, df1, by="id")
```



# anti_join()
```{r}
anti_join(df1, df2, by="id")
```



# left_join()
```{r}
left_join(df1, df2, by="id")
```



# right_join()
```{r}
right_join(df1, df2, by="id")
```





# join function using real data sets

# load data sets

```{r}
inv_1<-read.csv("inv_1.csv")
inv_2<-read.csv("inv_2.csv")
head(inv_1)
head(inv_2)
```

# comined inventory by 🆔 
```{r}
combined_inv <-full_join(inv_1, inv_2, by="Product_ID") 
head(combined_inv)
```

# transform data
```{r}

combined_inv$Category <- as.factor(combined_inv$Category)
```
